action: Consider ivabradine for symptomatic HFrEF with heart rate >=70 bpm on maximally tolerated beta blocker
action_detail: For patients with symptomatic (NYHA class II-III) stable chronic HFrEF (LVEF <=35%) receiving GDMT including a beta blocker at maximum tolerated dose, in sinus rhythm with resting heart rate >=70 bpm, ivabradine can be beneficial to reduce HF hospitalizations and cardiovascular death

properties.context: add-on when HR >=70 bpm on max beta blocker

source_text: For patients with symptomatic (NYHA class II to III) stable chronic HFrEF (LVEF <= 35%) who are receiving GDMT, including a beta blocker at maximum tolerated dose, and who are in sinus rhythm with a heart rate of >= 70 bpm at rest, ivabradine can be beneficial (COR 2a, LOE B-R)

action: Consider digoxin for symptomatic HFrEF despite GDMT
action_detail: In patients with symptomatic HFrEF despite GDMT (or who are unable to tolerate GDMT), digoxin might be considered to decrease hospitalizations for HF. The benefit of digoxin in patients with HF remains controversial and GDMT should be optimized before considering digoxin.
source_text: In patients with symptomatic HFrEF despite GDMT (or who are unable to tolerate GDMT), digoxin might be considered to decrease hospitalizations for HF (COR 2b, LOE B-R)

action: Monitor serum digoxin concentration to avoid toxicity
action_detail: Serum digoxin concentration should be monitored. Risk of death is independently associated with serum digoxin concentration, with significantly higher risk observed at concentrations >=1.2 ng/mL and >=1.6 ng/mL. Target serum digoxin concentration should be kept below 1.2 ng/mL; optimal range is 0.5-0.9 ng/mL based on retrospective analyses.

source_text: Two retrospective analyses of large-scale clinical trials have shown a linear relationship between mortality and digoxin serum concentration... The risk of death was independently associated with serum digoxin concentration, with a significantly higher risk observed in those with concentrations >= 1.2 ng/mL and >= 1.6 ng/mL.

action: Monitor renal function during digoxin therapy
action_detail: Digoxin is renally cleared. Low doses (0.125 mg daily or every other day) should be used if the patient has impaired renal function. Monitor eGFR and creatinine to guide dose adjustments and prevent digoxin accumulation and toxicity.

action_detail: Electrolyte monitoring, particularly potassium, is important during digoxin therapy. Hypokalemia increases the risk of digoxin toxicity by enhancing binding of digoxin to the sodium-potassium ATPase. Maintain potassium in normal range (3.5-5.0 mEq/L) to reduce toxicity risk.
source_text: Digoxin is usually initiated at a low dose because higher doses are rarely required in the management of HF and are potentially detrimental. Risk of death was independently associated with serum digoxin concentration.

action: Initiate and maintain digoxin at 0.125-0.25 mg daily
action_detail: Digoxin therapy is commonly initiated and maintained at a dose of 0.125 to 0.25 mg daily. Low doses (0.125 mg daily or every other day) should be used initially if the patient is >70 years of age, has impaired renal function, or has low lean body mass. Higher doses (0.375-0.50 mg daily) are rarely used or needed.

action_detail: Clinical worsening after withdrawal of digoxin has been shown. Therapy with digoxin may either be continued in the absence of a contraindication or discontinued with caution. Abrupt withdrawal may lead to clinical deterioration.

action: Consider vericiguat for high-risk HFrEF with recent worsening
action_detail: In selected high-risk patients with HFrEF and recent worsening of HF already on GDMT, oral soluble guanylate cyclase stimulator (vericiguat) may be considered to reduce HF hospitalization and cardiovascular death. Patients should have LVEF <45%, NYHA II-IV, elevated natriuretic peptides (BNP >=300 pg/mL or NT-proBNP >=1000 pg/mL in sinus rhythm), and recent HF worsening.

action: Monitor natriuretic peptides to assess eligibility for vericiguat
action_detail: Patients considered for vericiguat should have elevated natriuretic peptides: BNP >=300 pg/mL or NT-proBNP >=1000 pg/mL if in sinus rhythm (higher cutoffs with atrial fibrillation). Patients in the highest quartile of NT-proBNP (>5314 pg/mL) did not benefit from vericiguat.
source_text: Patients with HFrEF in the VICTORIA trial had LVEF <45%, NYHA class II to IV, were on GDMT, with elevated natriuretic peptides (BNP >= 300 pg/mL or NT-proBNP >= 1000 pg/mL if in sinus rhythm; higher cutoffs with AF)
